primary.interpretation: The preregistered species-turnover hypothesis is rejected. Spatial rearrangement of complete local assemblages under the fixed-margin null does not reduce the explanatory sufficiency of individual species.

supported: Across all 16 fresh sites, at least one individual target species survived every distinct canonical world.
Pooling species never increased surviving-world fraction above the best individual species.
No strict emergent world was observed in which the guild survived but every eligible individual species failed.
Cross-species-only local support occurred at low frequency but did not create additional system-level world survival.
At ORNL, pooling taxa reduced world survival from 1.0 for the best individual species to 0.25 for the guild under the frozen all-positive support rule.
not_supported: Species turnover creates emergent community-level spatial continuity in this programme.
High taxonomic richness implies emergent connectivity.
The most abundant or most spatially widespread species is necessarily the same species as the best world-survival species.
The observed pattern establishes dispersal mechanisms or causal habitat filtering.
The result may be retuned by changing world thresholds, target taxa, null model, or site roster.
